source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payment statistics (PSD/PAY/PTN/PTT datasets)
why_relevant: Harmonised ECB payment statistics re-publish MNB-reported Hungarian series: number of cards, card payment transactions/values, ATM and POS terminal counts, contactless/e-commerce splits, per-country and per-PSP. Longest harmonised comparable history for HU card/ATM/POS.

source_name: ECB Payment statistics landing page & methodology (payment services, LVPS, retail payment systems)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer to dataset structure, PSD Regulation (ECB/2020/59) reporting scope, revision policy and release calendar — needed to interpret breaks in the Hungarian series and to know when new HU data lands.

source_name: ECB Payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, e.g. 2025 H1)
why_relevant: Narrative + headline tables released with each payment statistics vintage; gives EU-wide framing and occasionally names country outliers, useful to benchmark Hungary's card/ATM trends without recomputing.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics key indicators (PAY dataset)
why_relevant: Pre-computed per-capita and per-country key indicators (card payments per inhabitant, ATM withdrawals per inhabitant) — the fastest way to place Hungary against EU peers for a market-sizing narrative.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Structural financial indicators (SSI): credit institutions, branches, employees
why_relevant: Annual EU-wide structural banking data including Hungarian branch counts and institution numbers since 1997 — the denominator/context for ATM-network rationalisation and self-service migration arguments.

source_name: ECB Data Portal SDMX REST API (data-api.ecb.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Machine-readable access path for every ECB dataflow above; makes the whole ECB layer a low-cost recurring collection target rather than a manual download.

source_name: ECB SPACE — Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area
why_relevant: Best harmonised cash-usage-at-POS benchmark in Europe (share of cash by number/value, reasons for cash use). Hungary is NOT a survey country (euro area only), so it serves as a comparator baseline for MNB's own Hungarian payment-habits surveys, not as an HU data source.

source_name: Eurostat Data Browser (ISOC / digital economy and society statistics)
why_relevant: Hungarian household/enterprise indicators on internet banking, online purchasing, e-commerce turnover — the demand-side context for card/e-commerce payment growth. Available in an HU-language Statistics Explained layer.

source_name: Eurostat Statistics Explained — Hungarian-language article layer (/hu)
why_relevant: Rare case of a supranational aggregator publishing in Hungarian; gives the official HU terminology (e.g. 'infokommunikációs eszközök', 'internetes vásárlás') that maps EU dataset codes to Hungarian search terms for other workstreams.

source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI payments and financial market infrastructures (Red Book statistics)
why_relevant: Deepest global time series on cashless payments, cards, terminals and currency in circulation, downloadable as CSV/SDMX. Hungary is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so HU is expected to be absent or only partially covered — value here is peer benchmarking (PL, CZ via EU aggregates, and global comparators) rather than HU rows.

source_name: BIS CPMI Red Book methodology (CPMI d168) and country tables (d172 series)
why_relevant: Defines the Red Book indicator taxonomy (fast payments, non-bank PSPs, contactless) that ECB and MNB definitions are increasingly aligned to; essential for reconciling differing Hungarian figures across aggregators.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS)
why_relevant: Annual, MNB-reported HU access-point indicators: ATMs per 100,000 adults and per 1,000 km2, branches, and newer POS-terminal indicators with rural/urban splits — a long, comparable HU ATM density series (e.g. 62.80 ATMs per 100k adults in 2024).

source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) mirror of IMF FAS Hungary series
why_relevant: Stable, API-friendly mirror of the HU ATM-density series when data.imf.org is awkward to automate; useful as a redundancy path and for quick charting.

source_name: DBnomics — IMF/FAS and other aggregator mirrors
why_relevant: Open aggregator that normalises IMF, ECB, Eurostat and BIS series into one API; cheap fallback and cross-check layer for HU payment/ATM series when a primary portal changes structure.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex Database (2025 edition and back waves)
why_relevant: Nationally representative HU adult-level indicators on account ownership, card ownership and use, digital/merchant payments, and reasons for non-use — the only demand-side, cross-country-comparable behavioural dataset for Hungary, with waves 2011/2014/2017/2021/2024.

source_name: World Bank Open Data / DataBank (WDI + Global Financial Development)
why_relevant: Re-publishes IMF FAS ATM density and Findex indicators for Hungary in a clean API with long panels; the Global Financial Development metadata glossary documents exactly how each HU indicator is derived.

source_name: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (GPSS)
why_relevant: Central-bank-answered survey on national payment system infrastructure, oversight, instant payments and interoperability; contains Hungary-level structural facts (e.g. absence of a cheque clearing house) not present in transaction statistics.

source_name: EBA Register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2 (EUCLID PIR)
why_relevant: Authoritative EU-wide register listing every Hungarian-authorised PI/EMI, its MNB authorisation, services and passporting footprint — the actor map for the HU acquiring/payments competitive landscape, refreshed from national registers.

source_name: EBA/ECB Report on Payment Fraud (2024, 2025 editions)
why_relevant: Joint EBA/ECB harmonised card and credit-transfer fraud statistics by country. Important caveat: the 2025 edition explicitly excludes Hungary because HU data were not available across the full period — a material coverage limitation to record.

source_name: EBA Guidelines on fraud reporting under PSD2 (reporting framework)
why_relevant: Defines what MNB must collect from Hungarian PSPs and forward via EUCLID — tells you which HU fraud/card series will become available, at what granularity, and when.

source_name: Payment Institutions Register EU (paymentinstitutionsregister.eu) — third-party mirror
why_relevant: Commercial/community re-presentation of the EBA PIR with easier browsing and filtering; useful for quick HU PSP lookups but must never be treated as authoritative over EUCLID.
